Sequential AIPE Check for the Standardized Mean Difference

Source: R/seq_aipe_smd.R
seq_aipe_smd.Rd

Checks, with the data collected so far from two independent groups, whether enough observations are in hand for a confidence interval for the population standardized mean difference \(\delta = (\mu_1 - \mu_2)/\sigma\) that is no wider than a chosen width, without assuming normality and without a planning value for \(\delta\). This is the sequential accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) procedure of Kelley, Darku, and Chattopadhyay (2018).

Usage

seq_aipe_smd(group_1, group_2, width, conf_level = 0.95)

Arguments

group_1, group_2

Numeric vectors: the observations collected so far from the first and the second group. Each needs at least 4 observations, the two must have the same length (the procedure adds the same number of observations to each group at every stage), and missing or infinite values are an error.

width

The target full width of the confidence interval for \(\delta\) (\(\omega\) in the cited article): the upper limit minus the lower limit. A single positive number.

conf_level

The confidence level of the interval, a single number strictly between 0 and 1. Default 0.95.

Value

An object of class c("smsd_check", "data.frame") (see smsd_check_methods for its print(), summary(), and tidy() methods) with one row per quantity and columns term and value. The rows are, in order:

lower_limit

the lower confidence limit (NA when the variance estimate is not yet usable or the estimate cannot be computed; see the section below);

smd

the estimated standardized mean difference (group_1 minus group_2, in pooled standard deviation units; NA when neither group has any variation);

upper_limit

the upper confidence limit (NA whenever lower_limit is);

xi_squared

the estimated asymptotic variance \(\hat{\xi}_n^2\), at least \(n^{-3}\) (the bound itself when the estimate is not yet usable);

criterion_n

the per group sample size the stopping rule currently requires (at least current_n + 1 when the variance estimate is not yet usable or the estimate cannot be computed);

current_n

the current per group sample size.

The object also carries these attributes:

is_satisfied

TRUE when the stopping rule is met, otherwise FALSE; never NA, and always identical to current_n >= criterion_n;

method

the string "standardized mean difference";

current_n, criterion_n

the values in the rows of those names;

conf_level, width

the values supplied;

variance_unusable

TRUE when the raw variance estimate is zero, negative, or not finite (see the section below), otherwise FALSE;

notes

a character vector, empty unless something needs explaining.

Details

The function evaluates the stopping rule once and returns. The user collects the pilot sample (see seq_aipe_smd_pilot), calls seq_aipe_smd(), and, while the rule is not met, adds one or more observations to each group and calls it again. The function prints nothing and keeps no state.

Estimate. The standardized mean difference is \(d_n = (\bar{X}_{1n} - \bar{X}_{2n}) / s_{pn}\), with \(s_{pn}^2 = (s_{1n}^2 + s_{2n}^2)/2\) the pooled variance of the two groups of common size \(n\) (their Equation 24), computed by smd.

Stopping rule. Sampling stops at the first \(n\) (per group), at or after the pilot size, with $$n \ge \left\lceil \frac{4 z_{\alpha/2}^2}{\omega^2} \left(\hat{\xi}_n^2 + \frac{1}{n}\right) \right\rceil$$ (their Equation 22), where \(\hat{\xi}_n^2\) estimates the asymptotic variance of \(\sqrt{n}(d_n - \delta)\) from the sample means, the pooled variance, and unbiased estimates of the third and fourth central moments of each group (their Equation 27). The reported interval is \(d_n \pm z_{\alpha/2} \hat{\xi}_n / \sqrt{n}\) (their Equation 28). Whenever the rule is met, the width of that interval is at most width.

Correction to Equation 26. Equation 26 of the article, and the sample version printed under its Equation 27, omit a factor of \(1/2\) in the term that carries the third central moments. The package implements the corrected variance, $$\xi^2 = 2 - \frac{(\mu_1 - \mu_2)(\mu_{13} - \mu_{23})}{2 \sigma^4} + \frac{(\mu_1 - \mu_2)^2}{4 \sigma^6} \left(\frac{\mu_{14} + \mu_{24}}{4} - \frac{\sigma^4}{2}\right),$$ where \(\mu_{kj}\) is the \(j\)th central moment of group \(k\). The two forms differ only when the means differ and the third central moments differ; they agree when the groups have the same third central moment (in particular for symmetric distributions) and when the two means are equal. The authors' correction is posted at https://kenkelley.org/wp-content/uploads/articles/Kelley_Darku_Chattopadhyay_Equation_26.pdf and is installed with the package, at the path returned by

system.file("eq26_correction.pdf", package = "SMSD")

What the guarantee is. The width guarantee is exact. The coverage guarantee is asymptotic: the coverage of the interval approaches conf_level as width shrinks, and so as the final sample size grows (their Theorem 4). In simulated studies with a 95% interval, a true \(\delta\) of 0.5, and one observation per group added at each stage, coverage was 0.952 at width = 0.4 (6,000 studies, about 200 per group at the end) and 0.946 at width = 0.2 (2,000 studies, about 790 per group) for normal data, and 0.944 and 0.949 for right skewed data (a standardized chi square distribution with 3 degrees of freedom); the Monte Carlo standard errors are 0.003 and 0.005. The variance estimate was never zero, negative, or below its lower bound in these studies. At a wide target the final sample is small, and coverage falls short for skewed data and, to a lesser degree, for a large \(\delta\): at width = 0.8 (10,000 studies each, about 50 to 105 per group at the end) coverage was 0.950, 0.946, and 0.943 for normal data and 0.926, 0.926, and 0.919 for the skewed data at \(\delta\) of 0.5, 1, and 2. Use seq_aipe_smd_sensitivity to study other conditions before collecting data.

A group with no variation. When every observation in one group is the same (values that agree to ten significant digits count as the same) while the other group varies, the estimate is still reported, but the variance estimate is not yet usable: the variance of that group has not been estimated, and the pooled standard deviation rests on the other group alone, so that it is too small and the estimate too large in size. The check reports the rule as not met and a note names the group (see the section below), as seq_aipe_c and seq_budget do with a constant group. In simulated studies of a 5 point item with 70% of one group's answers at the top of the scale (\(\delta = 1.08\), width = 1.5, 4,000 studies), 2.4% of the studies would have stopped with that group constant, and 41% of their intervals covered \(\delta\); with the group treated as not yet estimated, coverage over all studies was 0.927 against 0.917. The price is paid where a group stays constant: for a binary outcome with proportions 0.30 and 0.02 (width = 0.8, 2,000 studies) the mean final sample size was 64 per group against 33, and coverage 0.967 against 0.943. If a group shows no variation well past the pilot sample, reconsider the measure.

Estimates That Are Not Yet Usable

When the raw variance estimate is zero (exactly, or to within rounding error), negative, or not finite, which is common at small sample sizes for some effect sizes, or when the point estimate cannot be computed (a sample with no variation, where values that agree to ten significant digits count as equal), the check reports the stopping rule as not met, sets attr(out, "variance_unusable") to TRUE, and attaches a note that print() shows; see smsd_check_methods. This is a deliberate departure from the stopping rule as printed in the source articles, under which the lower bound \(n^{-3}\) would stand in for such an estimate and the rule would be met at once with an interval far narrower than requested; a positive estimate, however small, is used as the articles prescribe (the larger of it and \(n^{-3}\)).

References

Kelley, K., Darku, F. B., & Chattopadhyay, B. (2018). Accuracy in parameter estimation for a general class of effect sizes: A sequential approach. Psychological Methods, 23(2), 226–243. doi:10.1037/met0000127

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Maxwell, S. E., Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2008). Sample size planning for statistical power and accuracy in parameter estimation. Annual Review of Psychology, 59, 537–563. doi:10.1146/annurev.psych.59.103006.093735

See also

seq_aipe_smd_pilot for the pilot size and seq_aipe_smd_sensitivity to simulate the procedure before collecting data. In DMAR: ss_aipe_smd, the fixed sample size analog for when a planning value of \(\delta\) is available, and smd, the point estimator used here.

Other seq_aipe_smd: seq_aipe_sensitivity, seq_aipe_smd_pilot()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu, Francis Bilson Darku fbilsond@nd.edu, Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in

Examples

# Does a training program raise employee engagement (rated 1 to 7)? The
# aim is a 95% confidence interval for the standardized mean difference
# that is no wider than 0.60.
set.seed(113)
m <- seq_aipe_smd_pilot(width = 0.60)
trained <- rnorm(m, mean = 4.9, sd = 1)
control <- rnorm(m, mean = 4.5, sd = 1)
out <- seq_aipe_smd(trained, control, width = 0.60)
out
#> Sequential check (standardized mean difference)
#> 
#>   Current n       : 7
#>   Criterion n     : 91
#>   Target width    : 0.6
#>   Confidence level: 95%
#>   Coverage        : asymptotic; assess with sensitivity analysis
#> 
#>   lower_limit       : -1.143786
#>   smd               : -0.1011596
#>   upper_limit       : 0.9414664
#>   xi_squared        : 1.980884
#>   criterion_n       : 91
#>   current_n         : 7
#> 
#>   Stopping rule met: FALSE

# The rule is not met at the pilot. Add one employee to each group and
# check again, until it is.
while (!attr(out, "is_satisfied")) {
  trained <- c(trained, rnorm(1, mean = 4.9, sd = 1))
  control <- c(control, rnorm(1, mean = 4.5, sd = 1))
  out <- seq_aipe_smd(trained, control, width = 0.60)
}
out
#> Sequential check (standardized mean difference)
#> 
#>   Current n       : 85
#>   Criterion n     : 85
#>   Target width    : 0.6
#>   Confidence level: 95%
#>   Coverage        : asymptotic; assess with sensitivity analysis
#> 
#>   lower_limit       : 0.05840176
#>   smd               : 0.3564726
#>   upper_limit       : 0.6545434
#>   xi_squared        : 1.965901
#>   criterion_n       : 85
#>   current_n         : 85
#> 
#>   Stopping rule met: TRUE
